# AWS Landing Zone Design for Northshire County Council

*Generated by Kiro on 2025-06-27*

## Executive Summary

Northshire County Council requires a secure, compliant AWS landing zone to support their digital transformation initiatives and migration from on-premises data centers. This design provides a medium-complexity landing zone suitable for local government workloads handling OFFICIAL data, with support for citizen-facing digital services and internal systems. The design follows UK public sector best practices and aligns with NCSC Cloud Security Principles, Cyber Essentials Plus, and UK GDPR requirements.

## 1. Organization Profile

### 1.1 Organization Overview

- **Organization Name**: Northshire County Council
- **Organization Type**: Local Government
- **Scale**: Medium-sized council (approx. 2,500 employees, 350 IT users)
- **Geographic Scope**: UK only

### 1.2 Key Business Drivers

- Data center exit by Q3 2026 (leases expiring)
- Digital transformation of citizen services
- Cost reduction and operational efficiency
- Enhanced security posture and compliance

### 1.3 Current Environment

- **Cloud Maturity**: Low - exploratory AWS usage only
- **Existing AWS Footprint**: Single AWS account with test workloads
- **Key Systems**: Citizen services portal, planning applications system, social care case management, finance systems

## 2. Requirements Summary

### 2.1 Regulatory and Compliance Requirements

- NCSC Cloud Security Principles
- Cyber Essentials Plus certification
- UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018
- Local Government Digital Service Standard
- PSN Code of Connection (CoCo)

### 2.2 Security and Risk Requirements

- **Data Classification**: OFFICIAL, with limited OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE data
- **Security Controls Framework**: Aligned to NCSC Cloud Security Principles
- **Risk Tolerance**: Moderate - balanced approach between security and usability

### 2.3 Operational Requirements

- Small IT team (15 members) with limited cloud expertise
- 24x7 availability for critical citizen services
- Standard UK business hours (9-5) support for internal systems
- Monthly security patching cycle
- Annual budgeting cycle aligned to fiscal year (April-March)

### 2.4 Technical Requirements

- PSN connectivity for collaboration with other government entities
- Integration with existing Microsoft Active Directory
- Connection to on-premises systems during transition period
- UK region (London) hosting requirement for all services

## 3. Landing Zone Design

### 3.1 Account Structure

#### 3.1.1 Account Structure Diagram

```
Organization Root
├── Management Account
│   └── northshire-management
├── Security OU
│   ├── northshire-security
│   └── northshire-logging
├── Infrastructure OU
│   ├── northshire-shared-services
│   └── northshire-network
├── Non-Production OU
│   ├── northshire-development
│   └── northshire-test
└── Production OU
    ├── northshire-citizen-services
    ├── northshire-internal-systems
    └── northshire-sensitive-data
```

#### 3.1.2 Account Details

| Account | Purpose | Key Services | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| northshire-management | Organizations management | Organizations, Cost Explorer | Restricted access |
| northshire-security | Security services | GuardDuty, Security Hub, IAM | Security team access only |
| northshire-logging | Centralized logging | CloudTrail, Config, S3, Athena | Read-only for auditors |
| northshire-shared-services | Shared infrastructure | Directory Service, KMS, SSM | Platform team access |
| northshire-network | Network infrastructure | Transit Gateway, VPCs, Direct Connect | Network team access |
| northshire-development | Development environment | Developer services | Developer team access |
| northshire-test | Testing environment | QA services | QA team access |
| northshire-citizen-services | Citizen-facing services | Web applications, API Gateway | Public-facing workloads |
| northshire-internal-systems | Internal business systems | Finance, HR, operational systems | Internal workloads |
| northshire-sensitive-data | Social care/sensitive data | Case management systems | Higher security controls |

### 3.2 Organizational Units (OUs)

| OU | Purpose | Member Accounts | Key Policies |
|----|---------|----------------|--------------|
| Security | Security, audit, compliance | northshire-security, northshire-logging | Restrict service access, enforce encryption |
| Infrastructure | Shared technical services | northshire-shared-services, northshire-network | Network protection, resource sharing |
| Non-Production | Development, testing | northshire-development, northshire-test | Prevent production access, cost controls |
| Production | Live workloads | northshire-citizen-services, northshire-internal-systems, northshire-sensitive-data | Data protection, compliance controls |

### 3.3 Security Controls

#### 3.3.1 Preventative Controls

- All accounts enforce AWS IMDSv2 for EC2 instances
- SCPs to prevent public S3 buckets in all accounts
- Organization-wide restriction on unused regions (London and Ireland only)
- Enforced encryption at rest for all sensitive data services
- Prevention of privileged role creation outside of security account

#### 3.3.2 Detective Controls

- AWS Config enabled across all accounts with organization aggregator
- AWS Security Hub with CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark standard
- GuardDuty enabled organization-wide with centralized management
- CloudTrail organization trail with log integrity validation

#### 3.3.3 Responsive Controls

- Security Hub findings routed to IT Service Management platform
- GuardDuty findings trigger automated and manual responses
- CloudWatch alarms for security-relevant events
- AWS Systems Manager for automated patching and remediation

### 3.4 Network Architecture

#### 3.4.1 Network Architecture Diagram

[Network architecture diagram would be included here]

#### 3.4.2 Key Network Components

| Component | Purpose | Configuration |
|-----------|---------|---------------|
| Transit Gateway | Centralized network connectivity | Attached to all account VPCs, route propagation |
| PSN Connection | Government network access | Direct Connect via authorized PSN provider |
| VPC | Account-specific network isolation | /22 CIDR allocation per account from RFC1918 space |
| Network Firewall | East-west traffic inspection | Deployed in network account, centralized rules |
| Web Application Firewall | Public-facing protection | Deployed for citizen-facing applications |

### 3.5 Identity and Access Management

#### 3.5.1 Identity Providers

- AWS IAM Identity Center for federated access
- Integration with on-premises Microsoft Active Directory
- SAML 2.0 federation for console access

#### 3.5.2 Authentication Methods

- MFA required for all human users
- Conditional access policies based on device compliance
- AWS SSO for console access
- Programmatic access via IAM roles with temporary credentials

#### 3.5.3 Authorization Model

- Role-based access control aligning to job functions
- Permission sets aligned to job functions (finance, IT, developer, admin)
- Least privilege principle enforced through SCPs and IAM permissions boundaries

### 3.6 Logging and Monitoring

#### 3.6.1 Logging Architecture

- Centralized logging account with organization trail
- S3 bucket with appropriate lifecycle policies
- Athena for log querying
- Integration with existing SIEM for security monitoring

#### 3.6.2 Key Monitoring Components

| Component | Purpose | Configuration |
|-----------|---------|---------------|
| CloudWatch | Operational monitoring | Service metrics, custom dashboards |
| Security Hub | Security posture | CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, Operational Best Practices |
| AWS Config | Resource compliance | Managed and custom rules aligned to NCSC principles |
| CloudTrail | API activity monitoring | Organization trail with log file validation |

## 4. Governance Framework

### 4.1 Cost Management

- **Budget Structure**: Account-level budgets aligned to council service areas
- **Cost Allocation**: Tag-based cost allocation with mandatory tagging
- **Cost Optimization**: Savings Plans for predictable workloads, automated instance scheduling

### 4.2 Security Governance

- **Security Responsibility Model**: Shared responsibility documented for each team
- **Security Assessment Process**: Quarterly internal reviews, annual external assessment
- **Security Incident Response**: Integration with existing IT incident management

### 4.3 Compliance Management

- **Compliance Monitoring**: Automated via AWS Config and Security Hub
- **Audit Process**: Quarterly internal compliance reviews
- **Reporting Framework**: Monthly compliance reports to IT steering committee

## 5. Implementation Roadmap

### 5.1 Phase 1: Foundation (1-3 months)

- Establish management account and organizational structure
- Deploy security and logging accounts
- Implement core security services and controls
- Create network foundation with PSN connectivity

### 5.2 Phase 2: Expansion (3-6 months)

- Deploy non-production environments
- Implement CI/CD pipelines
- Establish workload onboarding process
- Pilot migration of low-complexity workloads

### 5.3 Phase 3: Migration (6+ months)

- Migrate citizen-facing digital services
- Migrate internal business systems
- Decommission on-premises infrastructure
- Optimize landing zone based on operational experience

## 6. Key Considerations and Recommendations

### 6.1 Key Design Decisions

| Decision | Options Considered | Selected Approach | Rationale |
|----------|-------------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Account structure | Basic vs. Standard vs. Comprehensive | Standard with service separation | Balance between separation and operational overhead |
| Identity provider | AWS IAM vs. Azure AD integration | Azure AD integration | Leverage existing council identity provider |
| Network connectivity | Internet VPN vs. PSN Direct Connect | PSN Direct Connect | Secure, reliable connectivity to government networks |
| Security Hub standards | AWS FSBP vs. CIS vs. Custom | CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark | Best alignment with Cyber Essentials Plus requirements |

### 6.2 Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|------------|
| Limited cloud expertise | High | High | AWS-led training program, partner engagement for implementation |
| Budget constraints | Medium | Medium | Phased approach with clear cost forecasting, reserved instances |
| Legacy application compatibility | High | Medium | Application assessment before migration, refactor where needed |
| Security compliance gaps | High | Low | Regular compliance scanning, remediation prioritization |

### 6.3 Dependencies

- Council approval of cloud strategy (complete)
- Procurement via G-Cloud framework (in progress)
- PSN provider engagement (scheduled)
- IT staff skills development (ongoing)
